added_failures_note: added failures retired by name in the reviewed node's done-when or manifest; total not capped

findings.text: follow-on: the sn-judge seat's registry entries (MODEL_SECTIONS and _MODEL_DEFAULTS) sit outside the declared write paths, which name pyproject.toml only, so the seat the goal requires cannot resolve without editing a path the fence excluded; the coordinator must widen the scope or accept the two paths at promotion.

follow-on: the monkeypatch target was retargeted from candidates.call_decisions to judgment.call_decisions, a second path outside the declared write scope, required because the deleted module-level name would otherwise leave tests/discovery with a failing reference.

follow-on: decide_one duplicates decide_batch's fail-soft transport handling (call, classify the exception, book the cost) instead of sharing the per-call unit the brief directs, so the two entry points can drift in how they classify a fault; the manifest records the deliberate decision that decide_batch's blanket swallow cannot be reused by a caller that must raise.

follow-on: baseline_suite carries completed:false and its base-arm.log is not a pytest run, so the "no added failures against base" claim rests on structural attribution (map.py byte-identical base..head) rather than a measured base arm; a later reader should treat the base half of the delta as unverified.

item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names tests/ids and tests/discovery with no added failures, a red candidate spend assertion when the shared booking line is removed, and get_model("sn-judge") resolving; the manifest records all three and I read each log it cites.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is one decisions owner plus a standard-names seat; imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:373 and imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:458 obtain answers through decide_one and no _call_judgment remains (grep over imas_codex/ returns line 289's prose only), and get_model("sn-judge") is registered in imas_codex/settings.py:150 and :190.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, the four commits, the gate command and its "1 failed, 800 passed, 13 skipped" result, the negative-control log and the base-arm limitation, and I confirmed the failing id is pre-existing.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are the two source files, pyproject.toml, five test files, the conftest fixture and the two evidence paths; the diff touches twelve files, ten inside that set and two outside it (imas_codex/settings.py, tests/discovery/test_decisions_key_skip.py), both disclosed in the manifest.

justifications.durability: tests/ids/test_candidate_judgment.py's spend assertions fail with KeyError under the negative control recorded in negative-control.log, and tests/discovery/test_judgment.py:291-295 imports the guard's target under a blocking hook with a positive control that reddens.

justifications.fit: the new names decide_one, _book_cost and DEFAULT_COST_STEP at imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:45-60 carry no plan or ticket label and match the "cost: Any | None" idiom already used across the module.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:373 and :458 route through decide_one in imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:60, so the private wrapper the goal retires is gone and the seat resolves at imas_codex/settings.py:190.
justifications.reuse: decide_one lives in the owner module imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py and _book_cost consolidates the booking both entry points share, but decide_one re-implements the call/classify/book shape of the per-call unit at judgment.py:176 rather than sharing it.
